description.value: The Wells Museum occupies one of the few surviving original Cariboo Gold Quartz Mining Company buildings, telling the story of prospector Fred Wells and the hard-rock gold rush that built the town in the 1930s. Run entirely by volunteers, it preserves artifacts, photographs, and historical sketches connecting Wells' mining heritage to its present-day community of artists, miners, and outdoor enthusiasts. Cyclists exploring the Barkerville corridor will find it a compelling stop that contextualizes the broader Cariboo gold country.

No mention of bike parking, washrooms, water refill, or any cyclist-specific amenity appears anywhere in the fetched content, so all required criteria and nearly all optional amenities must be null. OSM lacked address and phone fields, both of which are drawn from the website.

enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, operating seasonal attraction in a small Cariboo community on a popular cycling route near Barkerville; it offers genuine cultural interest to touring cyclists passing through Wells.
